description: Labelled expectations for sql_subquery_samples.json, checked by tests/test_workbook_fixture.py. Every case stays in the denominator; a row earns credit only when it parses strictly, is a valid input, changes, leaves no relational subquery and is proven.

fields.sha256: sha256 of the fixture file's bytes, CRLF line endings read as LF
fields.strict_parse: the lifter parsed the input without sqlglot recovery mode
fields.valid_input: DuckDB binds and runs the input, transpiled from BigQuery, on empty tables of duckdb_schema (SQLX: config and operations blocks skipped, ref("x") read as demo.dataform.x, when(incremental(), a, b) as b). This can refute validity; it does not establish BigQuery validity.
fields.remaining: relational subqueries left in the output (omitted means 0; a case that leaves one needs a remaining_reason)
fields.verification: apply_rule('lift_subqueries', sql).verification.status: proven, unchanged, unproven, planner_checked or failed
fields.verification_before_sqlglot: the status expected instead when the installed sqlglot is older than version (CI runs the 26.0.0 floor)

cases.invalid_reason: selects customer_id from the CTE regions, whose only output column is region
cases.verification_reason: BigQuery would reject the input (the CTE regions has no customer_id column), so a rewrite of it is refused rather than proven

cases.unchanged_reason: MERGE USING subquery is not lifted: only FROM and JOIN subqueries are relation subqueries
UPDATE cannot start with WITH in BigQuery, and a subquery directly in UPDATE ... FROM has no query scope to lift into
cases.remaining_reason: the UPDATE ... FROM subquery stays inline: BigQuery rejects WITH before UPDATE (Unexpected keyword UPDATE)
cases.verification_reason: the rule leaves a relational subquery, so apply_rule reports the unchanged output as failed

cases.unchanged_reason: the FROM subquery sits inside an EXISTS and reads an unqualified column (customer_id) that, without a schema, may belong to the enclosing query; a top-level CTE could not see it
cases.remaining_reason: the subquery inside EXISTS stays in place because its unqualified column may be correlated
cases.verification_reason: the rule leaves a relational subquery, so apply_rule reports the unchanged output as failed

cases.invalid_reason: HAVING on an outer query that has neither GROUP BY nor an aggregate; region and order_count are not grouped
cases.verification_reason: BigQuery would reject the input (HAVING with no GROUP BY and no aggregate), so a rewrite of it is refused rather than proven
the WHERE holds ${when(incremental(), ...)}, which can expand to any SQL (including a reference to the alias or CTE the lift renames), so the change stays unproven until the SQLX is compiled
